rounds.text: Destiny Logistics & Infra Ltd carries a valuation that is completely detached from its underlying returns, trading at an exorbitant price-to-earnings multiple of 66.4 [E1] despite generating a mediocre return on capital employed of 8.7% [E6] and a meager return on equity of 6.7% [E7]. This fundamental disconnect is underscored by a price-to-book ratio of 3.04x on a book value of ₹ 33.2 per share [E2]. Furthermore, a discounted cash flow valuation establishes an intrinsic value of only ₹ 62 per share against the prevailing market price of ₹ 101 [E33], resulting in a severe negative margin of safety of -62.6% [E34]. The reverse DCF model confirms that the current market price aggressively prices in 24.8% earnings growth, vastly exceeding the realistic 18.0% baseline assumption [E35], while offering zero yield to shareholders through its 0.00% dividend rate [E4]. Conceded: the company has demonstrated impressive compounded sales growth of 51% over 5 years [E8]. Nevertheless, with the stock pinned just 2% above its 52-week low [E5], the risk of multiple contraction far outweighs any historical top-line expansion [E62].

scorecard.note: Computed arithmetically from the citations that survived grounding — no model input.

evidence.fact: Price-to-book is 3.04x (price ₹ 101 on a book value of ₹ 33.2).
The stock sits 2% of the way up its 52-week range (100 low to 143 high).
Compounded sales growth over 5 years is 51%.
A discounted cash flow puts intrinsic value at Rs 62 per share against a market price of Rs 101.
That leaves a margin of safety of -62.6%.
A reverse DCF says today's price already implies 24.8% earnings growth, against the 18.0% the base case assumes.
